mcp.title: AI apps (MCP)
mcp.intro: Let AI apps such as Claude Code and Claude Desktop use this vault through the Model Context Protocol. They run Gumply on this computer; nothing goes over the network.
mcp.enabled: Let AI apps use this vault
mcp.accessReadHint: Search and read pages, tags, links and the graph.
mcp.accessAppendHint: Also create pages, add to the end of a page, and add cards to boards. Never changes what's already written.
mcp.accessEditHint: Also change and trash pages. Every change is kept in history and can be undone, but a note with misleading text could trick an AI into editing other pages. Keep “Read and add” unless you need this.
mcp.restartNote: After allowing more, restart the AI app's connection to Gumply. Allowing less takes effect at once.
mcp.claudeDesktopHint: Add this to {{path}}, then quit Claude Desktop completely and open it again:
mcp.npmHint: AI apps don't use your terminal's PATH, so the gumply command may not be found. Build Gumply's MCP server (npm run build -w @gumply/mcp), then reopen this dialog for a snippet with full paths.
mcp.appImageHint: This is the AppImage file's own path. If you move or rename it, copy the snippet again.
mcp.fuseWarning: This AppImage needs FUSE to start, and it isn't installed: run sudo apt install fuse3, or use the .deb.
mcp.macLocationHint: Move Gumply to the Applications folder and open it from there, then copy the snippet. A copy run from the disk image goes away when it's closed.

mcp.offNote: AI apps can't use this vault while this is off.

conflicts.title: Conflicts
conflicts.commandWords: conflicts sync copies syncthing dropbox nextcloud icloud onedrive
conflicts.intro: When two devices change the same page, your sync app keeps the other side as a copy beside it. Compare them, then keep one, the other, or both. Nothing is deleted: the side you don't keep goes to the Trash.
conflicts.empty: No conflicts. Everything is in sync.
conflicts.bannerOne: This page has a conflicting copy from {{device}}, {{date}}.
conflicts.bannerOneUnknown: This page has a conflicting copy from {{tool}}.
conflicts.copyBanner: This is a conflicting copy of “{{title}}”, made by {{tool}} on {{date}}.
conflicts.copyBannerNoDate: This is a conflicting copy of “{{title}}”, made by {{tool}}.
conflicts.readOnly: Copies are read-only, so they never become a third version.
conflicts.same: This copy is the same as the page.
conflicts.orphan: This is a conflicting copy, and the original page was deleted or renamed on another device.
conflicts.keptPage: Kept the page. The copy is in the Trash.
conflicts.keptCopy: Kept the copy. The page's version is in its history.
conflicts.keptBoth: Kept both: the copy is now “{{title}}”.
conflicts.removed: Removed the copy. It's in the Trash.
conflicts.changed: This changed while you were comparing. Check again.
conflicts.fileByHand: Resolve this in your file manager: keep one file and delete the other.
conflicts.possibleHint: iCloud, OneDrive and Google Drive copies look like ordinary pages. These have such a name and mostly the same text as a page beside them.
conflicts.notACopyDone: “{{title}}” won't be shown as a possible copy again.
conflicts.beforeConflict: Compare with the version before the conflict
conflicts.noChanges: The page and the copy are the same.
